chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Khalid from one of his men from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

I said, 'A man enters the bathhouse, and the owner of the bathhouse splashes hot water upon him, causing the hair of his head to wither and not grow back.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the complete wergild (blood money).'

key_terms.فَلَا يَنْبُتُ: And it does not grow back
key_terms.فَيَمْتَعِطُ: It withers / becomes loose and falls out

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for hair loss caused by hot water in a bathhouse according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the loss of head hair due to scalding in a bathhouse constitutes a significant injury warranting the full *diyah* (blood money). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the value of physical integrity and the liability of service providers for negligence, distinguishing it from lesser injuries that might only require partial compensation.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Khalid, from one of his men, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I said, ‘The man enters the (public) baths, so the owner of the baths splashes hot water upon him, so the hair of his head withers away, so it does not grow back’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is the complete wergild’.
